parts:
Hi all,

In the attached nimble code, I defined the number of clusters, "Ke," as the number of unique values in the vector returned by "dCRP." However, an error occured, indicating that "Ke" was not found. Does anyone know what happened? 

Also, the "Ke" was computed by calling two R functions:

Runique <- nimbleRcall (
  function (x=double (1) ){}, Rfun="unique",
  returnType=double (1))

Rlength <- nimbleRcall (
  function (x=double (1) ){}, Rfun="length",
  returnType=double (1))

Ke <- Rlength(Runique(groupe[1:N]))

Is this the right way to call R functions in nimble?

Thanks a lot for your time.


Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Error in nm_seq_noDecrease((1), (Ke)): object 'Ke' not found
parts:
hi Chris, a bit of follow-up to Perry's comments.

For a CRP model you should either define taue.mix to have length equal to the maximum number of clusters, which is N, or you could set it to some _fixed_ smaller number, in which case Nimble's MCMC will warn you if the MCMC tries to use more clusters than the fixed number (and you could then bump the number up and try again). Setting to N is safe, but involves overhead/inefficiency in various ways from having the N nodes in the model. We have some discussion of the issue here.

-chris

Your suggestion is definitely enlightening to me. I will try to circumvent the issue.
